profile.headline: Senior Bioinformatics Scientist & Scientific Software Engineer | Python, NGS/ONT, Benchling/LIMS, Cloud/HPC | Computational Biology
profile.jobTitle: Independent Bioinformatics Scientist & Scientific Software Engineer
profile.summary:
I build bioinformatics software that turns novel assays and complex biological data into validated, reproducible systems scientists can trust.

I am a senior bioinformatics scientist and scientific software engineer with 10+ years across clinical diagnostics, immuno-oncology, single-cell genomics, V(D)J analysis, long-read synthetic biology, and laboratory informatics. My work spans scientific requirements and data modeling through Python implementation, benchmarking, automated QC, visualization, documentation, and operational handoff.

Selected evidence:
• Co-designed Nanoplex, the Python/ONT verification pipeline for SCRIVENER, and analyzed data supporting a 2026 Cell Systems paper covering >5,000 DNA assemblies and constructs up to 81 kb.
• Built NGS/Sanger analysis software and Benchling chain-of-identity workflows for personalized T-cell therapy at PACT Pharma; a Dash application reduced routine plasmid-sequencing analysis from hours to minutes.
• Developed donor-derived cfDNA, scRNA-seq, and V(D)J workflows at CareDx, Bio-Rad, and Bristol Myers Squibb, and Python/Benchling migration tooling for Calico.
• Currently lead independent CGT-to-CORD research across 43 public perturbational datasets, with held-out evaluation, null models, provenance, and explicit limits on generalization and causal claims.

Core tools include Python, NumPy/SciPy/pandas/Polars/scikit-learn, Bash/Linux, Git, NGS/ONT, Benchling LIMS/ELN/API, cloud/HPC, Docker, Dash/Plotly, statistical modeling, and reproducible data pipelines. I use coding and reasoning agents as supervised engineering collaborators while retaining responsibility for architecture, biological interpretation, security, and scientific claims.

Open to remote U.S. roles in bioinformatics, computational biology, and scientific software engineering.

positions.title: Independent Bioinformatics Scientist & Scientific Software Engineer
positions.description:
Developing CGT-to-CORD, an independent computational-biology program evaluating recurrent perturbation-response structure and its context dependence.

• Published an analysis-frozen, preprint-style web report spanning 43 perturbational transcriptomic datasets, with external CRISPR gene-fitness and TCGA tumor-state evaluations.

• Designed held-out tests, endpoint shuffles, strict study/context exclusions, and explicit claim boundaries to separate predictive association from causal or transportability claims.

• Built provenance-tracked Python/Colab workflows with versioned inputs, content hashes, run/release manifests, and claim-to-evidence ledgers.

• Use coding and reasoning agents as supervised engineering collaborators for specification, implementation, testing, review, and documentation while retaining responsibility for architecture, biological interpretation, and scientific claims.
positions.insights: Skills: Python · Software Development · Genomics · Scientific Computing · Computational Biology · Bioinformatics · Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS)

positions.title: Staff Software Developer
positions.description:
• Co-designed and implemented Nanoplex, the Python/ONT pipeline used to verify SCRIVENER DNA assemblies, integrating combinatorial-barcode demultiplexing, minimap2/samtools alignment, bcftools/Sniffles2 variant calling, SciPy read-length clustering, and automated QC and purity scoring on a 36-core cluster.
• Analyzed sequence-verification data supporting a Cell Systems study of more than 5,000 assemblies spanning 2–19 DNA blocks and constructs up to 81 kb; generated publication evidence, edited the manuscript, and coauthored the paper.
• Built Benchling API tools and data models for assembly planning, sample lineage, inventory and entity creation, and LIMS registration.
• Collaborated across R&D and software teams on scientific requirements, infrastructure, validation, and continuous-integration planning.

positions.title: Bioinformatics Engineer
positions.description: BacStitch has pioneered an advanced technology known as in vivo highly multiplexed barcoding for the assembly of long DNA sequences. This approach enables the efficient construction of large DNA molecules by incorporating unique DNA barcodes into individual genetic fragments and allowing for pooling of hundreds to thousands of plasmids for sequencing verification on Oxford Nanopore flowcells. This in vivo high-throughput barcoded-"stitching" process enables precise tracking and assembly of multiple DNA fragments simultaneously within living cells. By harnessing the power of highly multiplexed barcoding, BacStitch reduces the costs of DNA assembly by orders of magnitude, facilitating the creation of complex genetic constructs with unparalleled speed, accuracy, and scalability. This technology holds immense promise for various applications in synthetic biology, genetic engineering, and biotechnology, potentially paving the way for groundbreaking advancements in the manipulation and understanding of genetic information.

• Worked with the software-engineering team on a company-wide LIMS integration.

positions.title: Bioinformatics Data Scientist
positions.description:
As a Bioinformatics Data Scientist at PACT Pharma, I managed databases and LIMS for R&D teams, developed a Sanger sequencing web application, and contributed to creating patient-tailored cancer-targeting T-cell therapy. 

• Managed database and LIMS for R&D teams at PACT Pharma using Benchling
• Developed a Sanger sequencing web application that automated gene-edited plasmid sequencing QC process
• Contributed to the creation of patient-tailored cancer-targeting T-cell therapy
Bioinformatics Data Scientist with database and LIMS management expertise, software development, and personalized cancer immunotherapy. At PACT Pharma, I managed R&D databases and LIMS, developed a custom Sanger sequencing web application, and contributed to pioneering patient-specific T-cell therapy to target solid tumors.

• Principal database/LIMS manager for R&D teams, leveraging Benchling for data capture, standardization, and cross-functional computational needs • Developed a Sanger sequencing app (10K+ lines of Python code), reducing QC analysis from hours to under 1 minute with automated, scalable, and user-friendly features for multi-sample processing • Supported data integration for immuno-oncology, blending advances in protein science, gene editing, and tumor immunology to enable first-of-its-kind, neo-epitope targeting T-cell therapy

PACT Pharma's platform engineers next-gen synthetic TILs (tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes) from patients’ autologous T cells, programming them to identify, infiltrate, and destroy tumor cells displaying unique neo-epitopes. This personalized immunotherapy is designed for rapid manufacturing from biopsy to reinfusion, creating tailored treatments for individual cancer patients.

positions.title: Bioinformatics Pipeline Developer
positions.description:
Scientific computing analysis & custom software development for I-O (immuno-oncology) focused bioinformatics. [Contract Consultant]

Integrated a combination of open source bioinformatics and data science tool resources with custom python programming, shell scripting, and Docker-containerized Linux environment mgmt. for cloud-based, high-performance computing of V(D)J-gene rearrangement genomics analyses (i.e., as enabled from high-throughput [near-exhaustive] NGS investigation of "Antigen Receptor Repertoires"). Many millions of V(D)J gene-recombined antibody sequences are possible from the constituent human germline alleles alone, demanding a depth of molecular survey with immensity excellently suited for recent NGS capabilities. 

Such "repertoires" of antibody sequences are now often derived, for example, from murine human-transgenic lymphocytes, phage display screens, synthetic rational designs, and other technologies capable of producing humanized or fully human (i.e., least likely immunogenicity) IgG proteins with clinical potential as immunotherapeutic mfg.'d mAbs.
positions.insights: Skills: Python · Cloud Computing · Data Visualization · Git · Algorithms · Genomics · Scientific Computing · Computational Biology · Web Applications · Data Science · Docker Products · Bioinformatics · Biotechnology · NGS · Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS)

positions.title: Bioinformatician II - Sequencing Analysis
positions.description:
As my primary project, I created a working framework for a secondary and tertiary custom NGS pipeline for a single-cell whole-transcriptome unique-molecular-barcoded RNA-Seq assay leveraging Bio-Rad’s proprietary droplets fluidics technology for the cell isolation and polyA-tail capture, along with Illumina’s Nextera™ technology for library preparation. I developed an advanced cloud computing network on Microsoft Azure, and genomically mapped samples in parallel using a scaling-VM highly-multicore cluster architecture. For tertiary analysis, I used database genome-wide GENCODE annotation (as recommended by STAR) and wrote assay-specific barcode deconvolution algorithms to calculate digital transcript counts and then fed these into various dimensionality reduction functions from Python Scikit-learn, such as k-means clustering, PCA, MDS, and t-SNE.  To create high-quality, reproducible & large-scale visualizations I designed an automated workflow for outputting pdf reports using the Python Data Science stack (namely matplotlib, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, Bokeh, & Seaborn) in a Conda-controlled Azure/Ubuntu-Linux environment. 

Then, cloud-side, I SSH port-forward a Jupyter Python3 server for: i) a local powerful browser-interface to the remote VM's, & ii) dual functioning as an archivable/presentable record.  This Notebook-UI setup then easily facilitates rapid live reproduction of numerous incrementally varying 2-3D visual perspectives  of the samples, revealing more from the combinatorial spectrum of possible parameter tunings of the ML algorithms vs. more biased narrower view (e.g., # of principle components,  # of k-means clusters, and # of features/dimensions to select for). Both the simpler linear decomposition method (PCA) and the more complex nonlinear t-Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) manifold-based method yield their own complementary hidden insights into the relationships between individual cells and the 
ontology of RNA-defined cell types.

positions.title: Bioinformatics Analyst
positions.description:
Python-centric R&D software engineering for data analysis & visualization of NGS cell-free DNA results, implementing both standard and custom tools with a focus on assay performance characterization, error correction by integration of various QC-filtering algorithms, and testing of protocol adjustments. 
 
In line with CAP, ACMG, AMP, & ASHG NGS development professional guidelines, orthogonal bioinformatic analysis helps substantiate high confidence in the accuracy and precision of the assay (e.g., exhaustive "truth" confirmation for panel-overlapping SNVs in NIST reference standards ran in-house; in silico artificially mutated amplicons assessing background noise). Without prior genotyping of the highly heterogeneous tetraploid genome mixture that constitutes the circulating cfDNA in Tx patients, complex interpretation of single-nucleotide genotype differences is required. By only considering SNPs known from population studies to have approximately 50% MAF in all humans, binomial modeling assumptions combined with Mendelian principles reveal highly accurate HTS measurement of allele frequency distributions (LOB=0.1%/LOD=0.2%) that directly correlate with varying levels of donor-derived cfDNA (see Python analysis  below).

Illumina NGS platforms [ultra-deep targeted sequencing (MiSeq) & WGS/WES/RNA-Seq (HiSeq)] |  GNU Linux Unix env.'s, bash shell scripting , SQL databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, NoSQL), NumPy, SciPy, Pandas / R (DataFrame analysis), Jupyter Notebook | Custom data visualization (Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly, ggplot2): in-depth changes to default settings for publication-quality figures (e.g., AMP Journal of Molecular Diagnostics, Grskovic et al 2016*) | Translation of custom bioinformatics tools into Django web server / SQL database framework for rapid, click-to-execute generation of data analysis reports available on-demand across teams by automatic detection and upload of new sequencing data.

*[http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.jmoldx.2016.07.003]

positions.title: Research Associate — Bioinformatician
positions.description: Performance of a MiSeq library preparation assay for PCR-based quantification of donor-derived cell-free DNA independent of prior genotyping of donor/recipient pairs in transplant patients. Bioinformatic data analysis and visualization of NGS output, including secondary and tertiary pipeline development and computational biology research.

positions.description:
Contributed to research projects in three molecular biology labs at UCSC:

   - Single-cell RNA-Seq of an in vitro human breast cancer cell line with developed drug resistance & RNAi transfection knockdown of putative driver targets (with Dr. Nader Pourmand, Prof. Biomolecular Engineering, UCSC Genome Sequencing Center, Nanotechnology Gene Applications) 
[M.Sc. Graduate Capstone project, 2014]

    - Nanopore sequencing & potential application of heterologous protein expression in halophilic archaea yielding highly salt tolerant DNA Polymerase motors (with Dr. Mark Akeson, Prof. & Chair Biomolecular Engineering) 
[Undergraduate Senior Thesis, 2012-2013]

   - Recombinant chromosome protein dynamics during meiotic cell-cycle regulation and dysfunction in C. elegans (with Dr. Needhi Bhalla, Assoc. Prof. Genetics, Molecular Cellular and Developmental Biology)
[Undergraduate research, chemical mutagenesis & manual LoF/GoF genetic screening via genome engineered epistatic phenotype markers, 2011-2013]

experience.title: Bioinformatician II - Sequencing Analysis
experience.description:
As my primary project, I created a working framework for a secondary and tertiary custom NGS pipeline for a single-cell whole-transcriptome unique-molecular-barcoded RNA-Seq assay leveraging Bio-Rad’s proprietary droplets fluidics technology for the cell isolation and polyA-tail capture, along with Illumina’s Nextera™ technology for library preparation. I developed an advanced cloud computing network on Microsoft Azure, and genomically mapped samples in parallel using a scaling-VM highly-multicore cluster architecture. For tertiary analysis, I used database genome-wide GENCODE annotation (as recommended by STAR) and wrote assay-specific barcode deconvolution algorithms to calculate digital transcript counts and then fed these into various dimensionality reduction functions from Python Scikit-learn, such as k-means clustering, PCA, MDS, and t-SNE.  To create high-quality, reproducible & large-scale visualizations I designed an automated workflow for outputting pdf reports using the Python Data Science stack (namely matplotlib, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, Bokeh, & Seaborn) in a Conda-controlled Azure/Ubuntu-Linux environment. 

Then, cloud-side, I SSH port-forward a Jupyter Python3 server for: i) a local powerful browser-interface to the remote VM's, & ii) dual functioning as an archivable/presentable record.  This Notebook-UI setup then easily facilitates rapid live reproduction of numerous incrementally varying 2-3D visual perspectives  of the samples, revealing more from the combinatorial spectrum of possible parameter tunings of the ML algorithms vs. more biased narrower view (e.g., # of principle components,  # of k-means clusters, and # of features/dimensions to select for). Both the simpler linear decomposition method (PCA) and the more complex nonlinear t-Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) manifold-based method yield their own complementary hidden insights into the relationships between individual cells and the 
ontology of RNA-defined cell types.

positions.title: Bioinformatics Analyst
positions.description:
Python-centric R&D software engineering for data analysis & visualization of NGS cell-free DNA results, implementing both standard and custom tools with a focus on assay performance characterization, error correction by integration of various QC-filtering algorithms, and testing of protocol adjustments. 
 
In line with CAP, ACMG, AMP, & ASHG NGS development professional guidelines, orthogonal bioinformatic analysis helps substantiate high confidence in the accuracy and precision of the assay (e.g., exhaustive "truth" confirmation for panel-overlapping SNVs in NIST reference standards ran in-house; in silico artificially mutated amplicons assessing background noise). Without prior genotyping of the highly heterogeneous tetraploid genome mixture that constitutes the circulating cfDNA in Tx patients, complex interpretation of single-nucleotide genotype differences is required. By only considering SNPs known from population studies to have approximately 50% MAF in all humans, binomial modeling assumptions combined with Mendelian principles reveal highly accurate HTS measurement of allele frequency distributions (LOB=0.1%/LOD=0.2%) that directly correlate with varying levels of donor-derived cfDNA (see Python analysis  below).

Illumina NGS platforms [ultra-deep targeted sequencing (MiSeq) & WGS/WES/RNA-Seq (HiSeq)] |  GNU Linux Unix env.'s, bash shell scripting , SQL databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, NoSQL), NumPy, SciPy, Pandas / R (DataFrame analysis), Jupyter Notebook | Custom data visualization (Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly, ggplot2): in-depth changes to default settings for publication-quality figures (e.g., AMP Journal of Molecular Diagnostics, Grskovic et al 2016*) | Translation of custom bioinformatics tools into Django web server / SQL database framework for rapid, click-to-execute generation of data analysis reports available on-demand across teams by automatic detection and upload of new sequencing data.
